by-components.description: Every organizational user is uniquely identified by a named Okta account; shared and generic accounts are prohibited by the Access Management Standard. Okta authenticates users with SAML single sign-on and enforces phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication at each login to AWS, GitHub and the admin console. Each session token issued to an application carries the user's unique identifier, so processes acting on behalf of the user are associated with that identity. The IAM team owns the Okta tenant and reviews the authentication policy quarterly; Okta system logs are streamed to Splunk in real time and retained for 13 months as evidence.

The Security Operations team reviews and analyzes audit records in Splunk daily for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity, such as account takeover, privilege escalation, impossible travel and mass export of payment data, and assesses the potential impact of each alert. Correlation searches raise alerts in real time and each review is recorded in a ServiceNow ticket. Findings are reported to the CISO and the system owner weekly, and within 24 hours for high severity incidents. The SOC manager adjusts the level of audit review and analysis when threat intelligence or law enforcement information indicates a change in risk, and records the change in the detection backlog.
Accounts are reviewed periodically as needed to make sure they are still appropriate.
